category: List the key vaccines included in the EPI schedule
statement: A medical officer at a Basic Health Unit is reviewing the constituents of the Pentavalent vaccine currently administered under Pakistan's Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI). Which combination of antigens correctly identifies the five diseases targeted by this single injection?
options: Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Tuberculosis, and Polio
Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae type b
Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Pneumococcus, and Hib
Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Typhoid, and Hepatitis B
Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Hepatitis B, and Rotavirus
correctOption: Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Hepatitis B, and Haemophilus influenzae type b
optionExplanations: Incorrect. Tuberculosis (BCG) and Polio (OPV/IPV) are distinct vaccinations in the schedule. BCG is given at birth, and Polio is given at birth, 6, 10, 14 weeks, and 9 months.

Correct. The Pentavalent vaccine, introduced in Pakistan in 2009, is a conjugate and combination vaccine that protects against these five specific bacterial and viral pathogens in a single 0.5ml intramuscular dose.
Incorrect. Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine (PCV) is a separate injection given at the same 6, 10, and 14-week visits as Pentavalent, but it is not contained within the Pentavalent syringe.
Incorrect. Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine (TCV) is a separate vaccine introduced into the routine schedule in 2022, administered specifically at 9 months of age, and is not part of the Pentavalent series.
Incorrect. While Rotavirus is part of the EPI schedule at 6 and 10 weeks, it is an oral vaccine administered separately, not part of the Pentavalent combination injection.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": Pentavalent vaccine combines protection against five diseases: diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B and Haemophilus influenzae type b.

category: Evaluate the role of healthcare workers, community leaders, and families in promoting immunization
coreConcept: Overcoming Vaccine Hesitancy through Community Engagement
statement: A village experiences a surge in refusals for the HPV vaccine following rumors about its effect on future fertility. The local vaccinator is unable to convince the parents. Which intervention strategy, involving community leaders, is most consistent with Pakistan's EPI guidelines?
options: Forcibly vaccinating the children during school hours without community dialogue
Closing the local vaccination center until the community demand increases spontaneously
Engaging religious leaders and respected local figures to address rumors in culturally acceptable language
Increasing the supply of Pentavalent vaccine to the local fixed center
Replacing all local healthcare workers with staff from different provinces
correctOption: Engaging religious leaders and respected local figures to address rumors in culturally acceptable language
optionExplanations: Forcible vaccination is not advocated; the program relies on social acceptability, trusted communication, and community participation for sustained success.
Closing services would leave the population vulnerable and is the opposite of the EPI goal to extend services to difficult-to-reach groups and maintain demand.
This is correct; when technical experts (vaccinators) face mistrust, local figures and religious leaders can bridge the communication gap and restore public confidence.
Increasing the supply of a different vaccine (Pentavalent) does not address the specific rumors and hesitancy surrounding the HPV vaccine.
Replacing staff does not address the underlying misinformation; it may even increase mistrust if the new staff is unfamiliar with local customs.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": Religious leaders, teachers, local representatives, doctors, community organizations, media personnel and respected local figures can explain the purpose of vaccination in culturally acceptable language, address rumours and misinformation and encourage families to attend vaccination sessions.

category: Describe enhance vaccination uptake
statement: When comparing strategies to reach 'zero-dose' children in underserved Pakistani settlements, which operational approach provides the most significant contrast to the continuous base of fixed-site services?
options: Annual-only catch-up sessions for urban populations
Passive surveillance at district headquarters
Outreach and mobile vaccination teams targeting high-risk areas
Mass media campaigns without local site support
Reliance on tertiary hospital referrals for routine doses
correctOption: Outreach and mobile vaccination teams targeting high-risk areas
optionExplanations: Annual sessions are insufficient because new birth cohorts enter the population daily, requiring continuous routine services or frequent outreach to maintain herd immunity.
Passive surveillance is a method of monitoring disease, not a service delivery model for enhancing vaccine uptake in underserved areas.

Outreach and mobile services actively seek out populations with geographic or social barriers, whereas fixed sites require the community to come to the facility, making them complementary but distinct.
Mass media can create demand, but without localized delivery (outreach/fixed sites), it cannot convert that demand into actual vaccination uptake.
Referral systems often fail in underserved areas due to the travel and cost barriers that the outreach model is specifically designed to circumvent.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": Fixed facilities alone cannot achieve equitable coverage. Outreach teams therefore take vaccination services closer to settlements that are distant from facilities, while mobile approaches are particularly useful for remote populations

category: Discuss recent developments in the EPI, Pakistan
statement: With the most recent additions and expansions as of 2022, the Federal Directorate of Immunization (FDI) in Pakistan now primarily aims to protect children against how many vaccine-preventable diseases?
optionExplanations: 8 diseases was the count after the addition of Hepatitis B and Pentavalent, but before the inclusion of PCV, Rota, TCV, and Rubella.
10 diseases is an undercount that misses the most recent additions like Rubella and Typhoid.
While the program continues to grow (with HPV for specific groups), the core infant EPI schedule described in the current curriculum targets 12 primary diseases.
The program started with 6 diseases in 1976/1978, but it has significantly 'expanded' since then.
The current 12 targeted diseases are: Tuberculosis, Polio, Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Hepatitis B, Hib, Pneumonia, Rotavirus Diarrhea, Typhoid, Measles, and Rubella.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": The present Federal Directorate of Immunization programme primarily aims to protect children from birth to 15 months of age against 12 vaccine-preventable diseases.

category: Discuss recent developments in the EPI, Pakistan
statement: Under the current Pakistani EPI schedule, the Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine is administered in two doses. At what ages are these doses typically scheduled?
options: 15 months and 5 years
9 months and 15 months
6 weeks and 10 weeks
14 weeks and 9 months
9 months and 12 months
correctOption: 9 months and 15 months
optionExplanations: 15 months is correct for the second dose, but the first dose must be given earlier (at 9 months) to protect the infant as maternal antibodies wane.
The standard routine EPI schedule in Pakistan requires the first MR dose at 9 months and a follow-up second dose at 15 months to close immunity gaps.
6 and 10 weeks are the timings for Pentavalent-1 and 2, OPV-1 and 2, PCV-1 and 2, and Rotavirus-1 and 2.
14 weeks is the timing for the third primary series and IPV-1; 9 months is correct for MR-1, but 14 weeks is too early for MR.
9 months is correct for the first dose, but the second dose is administered at 15 months, not 12 months, in the Pakistan national schedule.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": Pakistan’s routine MR schedule therefore gives the first dose at nine months and the second at fifteen months.

category: Identify the strategies employed to implement the EPI in various communities
statement: A mother in a peri-urban settlement presents her 7-week-old infant who has received no previous vaccinations due to a cultural 40-day home-confinement period. Following the EPI strategy for addressing barriers and catch-up immunization, which clinical action is most appropriate?
options: Administer BCG, OPV-1, Pentavalent-1, PCV-1, and Rotavirus-1 immediately to begin the catch-up process.
Withhold the Rotavirus-1 vaccine because it cannot be safely administered if the birth dose of OPV was missed.
Delay all vaccinations until the 10-week mark to ensure the infant is synchronized with the standard visit schedule.
Refer the child to a tertiary hospital as catch-up immunization cannot be performed at primary health centers.
Administer only BCG and OPV-0 as the child must complete the birth doses before starting any other series.
correctOption: Administer BCG, OPV-1, Pentavalent-1, PCV-1, and Rotavirus-1 immediately to begin the catch-up process.
optionExplanations: The strategy for implementing EPI in communities where children are 'missed' involves immediate catch-up. BCG is required for TB protection, and the 6-week doses (Penta-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, Rota-1) are already overdue and should be given.
There is no contraindication for Rotavirus-1 based on a missed OPV-0 dose; they are separate components of the expanded schedule.
The text specifically warns that 'inappropriate deferral creates further opportunities for dropout'; the child should be vaccinated as soon as they present to the service.
EPI implementation is decentralized; catch-up immunization is a core competency of local vaccinators at primary health centers and through outreach.
While birth doses are important, at 7 weeks the child is also eligible for the 6-week series; the strategy is to complete all due doses as soon as the child is identified.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": Missed children should be identified and brought back into the schedule so that the required doses can be completed. ... inappropriate deferral creates further opportunities for dropout. ... In 2026, round-the-clock birth-dose centres supported in Pakistani hospitals have been providing immediate vaccination...

category: Describe the goals and objectives of the Expanded Program of Immunization (EPI) in Pakistan
statement: Which operational objective of the EPI is specifically designed to convert the mere availability of vaccines into the actual and timely vaccination of the target population?
options: Ensuring vaccine quality, maintaining the cold chain, and improving public confidence
Maximizing the cost of each individual dose to ensure high-quality production
Restricting vaccination services to specialized tertiary care hospitals only
Eliminating the use of immunization cards to simplify the recording process
Limiting the number of vaccination visits to only one per lifetime
correctOption: Ensuring vaccine quality, maintaining the cold chain, and improving public confidence
optionExplanations: Option B is correct. Having the vaccine in the country is insufficient; it must be kept potent (cold chain), be safe (quality), and the public must want it (confidence) for actual vaccination to occur.
Option A is incorrect because the program aims for affordability and cost-effectiveness, not maximizing the price of doses.
Option D is incorrect because the objective is to bring vaccines closer to the community through primary health centers and outreach, not to restrict them to tertiary hospitals.
Option E is incorrect because accurate recording via immunization cards is a stated objective to monitor coverage and prevent dropouts.
Option C is incorrect because the EPI schedule requires multiple visits (at birth, 6, 10, 14 weeks, 9 and 15 months) to ensure adequate immunological priming and boosting.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": EPI also aims to ensure vaccine quality and safety, maintain an effective cold chain and vaccine supply system... improve public confidence and demand for vaccination. These activities convert the availability of vaccines into actual and timely vaccination

category: List the key vaccines included in the EPI schedule
coreConcept: Synergistic Polio Immunization (Mucosal vs. Systemic Immunity)
statement: A medical student is studying the synergy between Oral Poliovirus Vaccine (OPV) and Inactivated Poliovirus Vaccine (IPV) in Pakistan's polio-endgame strategy. What is the fundamental immunological mechanism justifying the concurrent use of both vaccines?
options: OPV induces local intestinal immunity to interrupt transmission, while IPV ensures strong systemic protection against paralytic disease.
IPV is required to prevent the reversion of attenuated OPV strains into vaccine-derived polioviruses in the gut.
OPV provides systemic IgG while IPV provides mucosal IgA in the oropharynx.
OPV and IPV are used together because IPV alone cannot induce any humoral immune response in infants.
The combination is used exclusively to reduce the number of clinic visits rather than for any immunological synergy.
correctOption: OPV induces local intestinal immunity to interrupt transmission, while IPV ensures strong systemic protection against paralytic disease.
optionExplanations: OPV (Sabin) replicates in the gut, inducing robust mucosal IgA which prevents the wild virus from shedding, thus breaking the chain of transmission. IPV (Salk) provides high serum titers of IgG to protect the CNS from viremia, preventing paralysis.

While IPV protects the individual from paralysis, it does not prevent the replication of OPV in the gut or its potential reversion; its role in the strategy is systemic protection during the transition phase.
This is incorrect because OPV is primarily responsible for the secretory IgA response in the intestine (mucosal immunity), while IPV is highly effective at boosting systemic IgG.
IPV is highly immunogenic and induces a strong humoral (antibody) response; the claim that it cannot induce a humoral response is physiologically false.
The use of both is a specific immunological strategy to maximize both individual protection (IPV) and community transmission interruption (OPV), not merely an operational convenience.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": OPV is valuable for inducing intestinal immunity and interrupting transmission, whereas IPV produces strong systemic protection against paralytic disease; the two are therefore used together as part of Pakistan’s polio-endgame strategy.

category: Identify the common barriers to immunization coverage in Pakistan
statement: Which national resource has been established in Pakistan to provide government-approved information and address rumors and misinformation regarding vaccination?
options: The Provincial Cold Chain Registry
The TCV National Dashboard
The Sehat Tahaffuz 1166 Helpline
The AEFI Clinical Manual
The FDI Microplanning Portal
correctOption: The Sehat Tahaffuz 1166 Helpline
optionExplanations: The Cold Chain Registry tracks equipment like refrigerators and solar power units, not public rumors.
Dashboards are for data visualization of coverage and disease trends, primarily used by managers and policymakers.
The 1166 helpline is a public-facing service designed specifically to counter misinformation, answer parent concerns, and provide schedule details.
The AEFI Clinical Manual is a technical guide for healthcare workers on how to treat and report adverse events, not a public communication channel.
The Microplanning Portal is an internal tool for health staff to plan routes and targets, not a public information helpline.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": Pakistan’s Sehat Tahaffuz 1166 helpline provides government-approved information about vaccination schedules, vaccine safety, rumours and the location of appropriate services

category: List the key vaccines included in the EPI schedule
statement: A 16-month-old child presents for vaccination. The record indicates the child received BCG/OPV-0 at birth, and the full set of recommended vaccines at 6 and 10 weeks. However, the 14-week, 9-month, and 15-month visits were missed. To catch up according to the current Pakistan EPI schedule, which specific vaccines are required to complete these missed milestones?
options: Pentavalent-3, OPV-3, PCV-3, IPV-1, TCV, and MR-1 only.
Pentavalent-3, OPV-3, PCV-3, IPV-1, a later routine dose of IPV, TCV, MR-1, and MR-2.
BCV booster, OPV-3, PCV-3, IPV-1, and TCV.
PCV-3, Rotavirus-3, TCV, MR-1, and MR-2.
Pentavalent-3, OPV-3, PCV-3, IPV-1, and MR-1 only.
correctOption: Pentavalent-3, OPV-3, PCV-3, IPV-1, a later routine dose of IPV, TCV, MR-1, and MR-2.
optionExplanations: This option neglects the mandatory second dose of Measles-Rubella (MR-2) required at 15 months and the second routine dose of IPV given at 9 months.

This is correct. It accounts for the completed 14-week primary series (Penta-3, OPV-3, PCV-3, IPV-1), the 9-month requirements (MR-1, TCV, and the second IPV dose), and the 15-month requirement (MR-2).
There is no 'BCG booster' in the routine EPI schedule. BCG is a single dose given at birth. This list also misses the MR and IPV-2 components required later in the schedule.
Rotavirus vaccine is only given at 6 and 10 weeks in the Pakistan schedule; there is no 'Rotavirus-3'. It also misses the Pentavalent-3 and OPV-3 required for the 14-week milestone.
This option misses the Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine (TCV), the second dose of IPV (administered at 9 months), and the second dose of MR (administered at 15 months).
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": At fourteen weeks, Pentavalent-3, OPV-3 and PCV-3 complete the primary infant series... while IPV-1 provides additional protection... At nine months, the child receives the first measles-rubella vaccine, MR-1, along with typhoid conjugate vaccine, TCV, and the later routine dose of IPV... At fifteen months, the child receives MR-2.

category: List the key vaccines included in the EPI schedule
coreConcept: Pentavalent vs. PCV Components and Indications
statement: When contrasting the protection provided by the Pentavalent vaccine versus the Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine (PCV) in the EPI schedule, which pathogen is uniquely addressed by the Pentavalent vaccine to prevent invasive childhood meningitis?
options: Streptococcus pneumoniae
Bordetella pertussis
Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)
Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Neisseria meningitidis
correctOption: Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib)
optionExplanations: Streptococcus pneumoniae is the target of the PCV vaccine, not the Pentavalent vaccine. While both cause pneumonia and meningitis, they are distinct pathogens covered by different vaccines.
Bordetella pertussis is indeed in the Pentavalent vaccine (the 'P' in DTP), but it causes Whooping Cough (a respiratory tract infection) rather than being a primary cause of bacterial meningitis.

Hib (Haemophilus influenzae type b) is one of the five components of the Pentavalent vaccine. It was a leading cause of childhood bacterial meningitis and pneumonia before its inclusion in the 2009 EPI expansion.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis is targeted by the BCG vaccine given at birth, not by the Pentavalent or PCV vaccines which target encapsulated bacteria.
Neisseria meningitidis (Meningococcus) is not currently part of the routine childhood EPI schedule in Pakistan as a standalone or combined antigen in the primary series.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": Pentavalent vaccine combines protection against five diseases: diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B and Haemophilus influenzae type b. Hib protection is important particularly against serious invasive infections such as meningitis and pneumonia.

category: Describe the goals and objectives of the Expanded Program of Immunization (EPI) in Pakistan
statement: The EPI aims to ensure 'vaccine quality and safety'. What is the critical mechanism used to maintain the biological potency of vaccines from the manufacturer to the point of administration?
options: The Cold Chain system
Microplanning and mapping
The Sehat Tahaffuz 1166 helpline
The Vaccine Logistics Management Information System (VLMIS)
Supplementary Immunization Activities (SIAs)
correctOption: The Cold Chain system
optionExplanations: The cold chain is the physical infrastructure (refrigerators, cold rooms, carriers) that prevents heat or freeze damage, ensuring the vaccine remains biologically active (potent).
Microplanning is a logistical planning tool for session management; it does not itself maintain the temperature of the vaccines.
The 1166 helpline is for public communication and information, not for the physical storage or transport of biological products.
VLMIS is a data management tool for stock and logistics; it tracks inventory but is not the physical system for temperature maintenance.
SIAs are delivery strategies (campaigns) to increase coverage, not a mechanism for maintaining vaccine potency.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": The cold chain is the system that keeps vaccines at their required temperatures from the manufacturer and central store through provincial and district stores to the vaccination site.

category: Identify the strategies employed to implement the EPI in various communities
statement: The Federal Directorate of Immunization in Pakistan identifies a specific primary target age group for protection against 12 vaccine-preventable diseases. What is this target group?
options: Children from birth to 15 months of age
Adolescent girls aged 9 to 14 years exclusively
Pregnant women and women of childbearing age only
Newborns within the first 24 hours of life only
All citizens above the age of 5 years
correctOption: Children from birth to 15 months of age
optionExplanations: The core EPI childhood schedule in Pakistan is designed to complete the primary series and initial boosters for 12 targeted diseases by the age of 15 months.
While HPV vaccination targets this group, it is a recent addition and not the primary target group for the conventional 12 vaccine-preventable diseases of the infant EPI.
EPI targets this group for tetanus protection, but they are not the primary target for the 12 childhood diseases mentioned (e.g., Polio, Rotavirus, PCV).
Newborns are a critical starting point (birth dose), but the 12-disease program extends well beyond the first 24 hours to 15 months.
EPI is specifically a targeted public health program for susceptible infants and women of childbearing age, not a universal program for all citizens above age 5.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": The present Federal Directorate of Immunization programme primarily aims to protect children from birth to 15 months of age against 12 vaccine-preventable diseases...

category: Identify the strategies employed to implement the EPI in various communities
statement: A public health officer identifies a cluster of 'zero-dose' children in a peri-urban settlement. According to EPI implementation strategies, which marker is used to classify these children, and what is the primary recommended action?
options: Failure to receive the first routine vaccine (BCG/OPV-0); implement targeted microplanning and outreach
Failure to receive Pentavalent-3; provide only health education to the caregivers
Failure to receive PCV-1; refer the family to a private pediatrician
Failure to receive MR-1 at 9 months; initiate immediate hospital admission
Failure to receive the TCV dose; wait for the next national mass campaign
correctOption: Failure to receive the first routine vaccine (BCG/OPV-0); implement targeted microplanning and outreach
optionExplanations: Zero-dose children are those who have never accessed routine immunization (marked by missing the first dose). The strategy to reach them involves microplanning (local mapping) and outreach services to bring vaccines to them.
Failure to receive Pentavalent-3 denotes a 'dropout' or 'partially vaccinated' child, not a zero-dose child, and requires tracing rather than just education.

PCV-1 is administered at 6 weeks; missing it makes a child under-immunized, but 'zero-dose' specifically tracks the absolute entry point into the system. Referral to private clinics does not address the systemic barrier identified in the settlement.
MR-1 at 9 months is a later dose; the marker for 'zero-dose' status is the failure to receive the very first routine vaccine at birth or shortly after.
TCV is a later vaccine in the schedule. Waiting for a mass campaign is insufficient for routine protection and ignores the need to integrate the child into the routine system.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": Particular attention is therefore given to zero-dose children, who have not received the first routine vaccine used as a marker of access to routine immunization... Microplanning converts national targets into workable local activities.

category: Identify the strategies employed to implement the EPI in various communities
statement: In the context of the 'polio-endgame strategy' implemented in various communities across Pakistan, what is the primary immunological rationale for the co-administration of Oral Poliovirus Vaccine (OPV) and Inactivated Poliovirus Vaccine (IPV)?
options: OPV induces intestinal immunity to interrupt transmission while IPV provides systemic protection against paralytic disease.
OPV provides systemic IgG while IPV provides mucosal IgA to stop fecal-oral shedding.
The combination is used solely to reduce the number of clinic visits required for full immunization.
IPV is used to sensitize the immune system while OPV acts as a booster for long-term memory.
OPV is administered only to newborns to prevent VAPP, whereas IPV is reserved for the 14-week visit.
correctOption: OPV induces intestinal immunity to interrupt transmission while IPV provides systemic protection against paralytic disease.
optionExplanations: The strategic implementation uses OPV to create a mucosal barrier in the intestine, which prevents the virus from replicating and being transmitted in the community, while IPV ensures high levels of circulating antibodies to prevent the virus from reaching the central nervous system.
This option incorrectly reverses the roles; OPV is the live-attenuated vaccine that primarily induces mucosal IgA in the gut, while IPV (inactivated) primarily induces systemic IgG.
The combination is driven by the immunological necessity of achieving both individual protection and community-wide interruption of transmission, not merely to reduce visit frequency.
While both induce memory, their primary strategic roles are differentiated by the location of the immunity (intestinal vs. systemic) rather than a sensitization-booster relationship.
OPV is given at birth (OPV-0) and subsequent visits; the reason for adding IPV at 14 weeks is to bolster systemic immunity as part of the eradication strategy.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": OPV is valuable for inducing intestinal immunity and interrupting transmission, whereas IPV produces strong systemic protection against paralytic disease; the two are therefore used together as part of Pakistan’s polio-endgame strategy.

category: List the key vaccines included in the EPI schedule
statement: An 11-month-old infant is brought to a rural health center in Sindh. The mother provides a history of the child receiving only 'birth drops' (BCG and OPV-0). According to the EPI schedule and recent expansions, which of the following sets of vaccines is most appropriate to initiate/administer during this visit to address both primary series gaps and recent disease-specific additions?
options: BCG, Pentavalent-1, and OPV-1 only
Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, Rotavirus-1, MR-1, TCV, and IPV-2
MR-1, TCV, and IPV-2 only
Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, and Rotavirus-1
Rotavirus-1 and MR-2 only
correctOption: Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, Rotavirus-1, MR-1, TCV, and IPV-2
optionExplanations: The child already received BCG at birth according to the history, so repeating BCG is unnecessary. Also, this fails to provide the age-appropriate MR and TCV vaccines.

Correct. In a catch-up scenario, the child should receive the first doses of the primary series (Penta-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, Rota-1) plus the vaccines due for their current age (9 months: MR-1, TCV, IPV-2) to ensure rapid protection against all 12 targeted diseases.
This ignores the fact that the child never received their primary series (Pentavalent, OPV-1/2/3, PCV, Rotavirus). You cannot skip the primary infant series just because the child reached 9 months.
This only addresses the 6-week requirements. Since the child is 11 months old, they are also eligible for the 9-month vaccines (MR-1, TCV, IPV-2) and should not wait further for them.
MR-2 is not due until 15 months. Providing MR-2 at 11 months is incorrect timing. Furthermore, this neglects the five pathogens in the Pentavalent vaccine and the typhoid protection (TCV).
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": At nine months, the child receives the first measles-rubella vaccine, MR-1, along with typhoid conjugate vaccine, TCV, and the later routine dose of IPV... The 12 diseases are childhood tuberculosis, poliomyelitis, rotavirus diarrhoea, pneumonia, diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, hepatitis B, meningitis... typhoid, measles and rubella.

category: Discuss recent developments in the EPI, Pakistan
statement: A public health officer is reviewing the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) records for a district in Sindh. According to the recent expansion timeline, in which year was the Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine (TCV) first introduced in the Sindh province of Pakistan?
optionExplanations: 2019 marks the historic first introduction of TCV in Sindh, making Pakistan the first country to introduce this vaccine into its routine immunization program following a massive XDR typhoid outbreak.
2022 is the year when TCV finally achieved nationwide coverage across all provinces of Pakistan, three years after the initial Sindh launch.

statement: Pakistan utilizes both Oral Poliovirus Vaccine (OPV) and Inactivated Poliovirus Vaccine (IPV) in its current schedule. Which of the following best describes the complementary immunological roles of these vaccines in the national 'polio-endgame' strategy?

category: List the key vaccines included in the EPI schedule
statement: A 14-week-old infant is brought to an EPI center in Balochistan. The mother reports the child received BCG and OPV-0 at birth but missed all subsequent appointments due to travel. Based on the current Pakistan EPI schedule, which set of vaccines should be administered at this visit to initiate the primary series?
options: Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, Rotavirus-1, and IPV-1
Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, and Rotavirus-1
Pentavalent-3, OPV-3, PCV-3, and IPV-1
Pentavalent-2, OPV-2, PCV-2, and Rotavirus-2
MR-1, TCV, and IPV-2
correctOption: Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, and Rotavirus-1
optionExplanations: While IPV-1 is normally given at 14 weeks, it is part of the 14-week *visit* for children who followed the schedule; the priority here is starting the primary series of Penta/OPV/PCV/Rota.

Correct. According to EPI principles, if a child misses their 6 and 10-week visits, they must start with the first doses of the series (Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, Rotavirus-1) even if they are chronologically 14 weeks old.
The child cannot receive 'Dose 3' if they have not yet received Dose 1 and 2. The primary series must be started sequentially.
The child has not received Dose 1 of these vaccines, so they cannot jump to Dose 2.
MR-1 and TCV are not due until 9 months; the child is only 14 weeks old.

Missed children should be identified and brought back into the schedule.

category: Identify the common barriers to immunization coverage in Pakistan
statement: Which indicator does the EPI program in Pakistan use as a fundamental marker to assess whether a child has had 'access' to routine immunization services?
options: Knowledge of the Sehat Tahaffuz 1166 helpline
Attendance at a school-based vaccination seminar
Receipt of the first routine vaccine (e.g., BCG or Penta-1)
Completion of the second dose of Measles-Rubella (MR-2)
Possession of a QR-linked digital vaccination card
correctOption: Receipt of the first routine vaccine (e.g., BCG or Penta-1)
optionExplanations: Helpline knowledge measures community awareness/demand, not the actual access to vaccine administration services.
Seminar attendance is an educational metric, not a clinical marker of immunization access.
The first dose (BCG at birth or Penta-1 at 6 weeks) is the global and national standard for measuring 'access'; if a child hasn't received this, they are 'zero-dose'.
MR-2 is an indicator of 'completion' or 'retention', not 'access', as it occurs at 15 months.
Digital cards are tools for record-keeping, but the marker of access is the biological administration of the first vaccine dose.

category: List the key vaccines included in the EPI schedule
statement: A public health survey in an urban slum identifies several 'zero-dose' children. Within the operational framework of Pakistan's EPI, how is a 'zero-dose' child specifically defined?
options: A child whose mother did not receive Tetanus-containing vaccine during pregnancy.
A child who has not received the first routine vaccine used as a marker of access (Pentavalent-1).
A child who has not received the second dose of Measles-Rubella vaccine by 15 months.
A child who has not received any vaccines, including those in supplementary campaigns.
A child who has received only birth doses (BCG/OPV-0) but no subsequent vaccines.
correctOption: A child who has not received the first routine vaccine used as a marker of access (Pentavalent-1).
optionExplanations: This refers to the tetanus status of the mother, not the zero-dose status of the child.

Correct. In global health and specifically in Pakistan's EPI, 'zero-dose' refers to children who have not received the first dose of the DTP-containing vaccine (Pentavalent-1 in Pakistan), which indicates a total lack of access to routine services.
Missing the second dose of MR makes a child 'partially vaccinated' or a 'defaulter,' not 'zero-dose.'
This is a general definition of 'unvaccinated,' but the EPI specifically uses a marker vaccine to define the metric for 'zero-dose.'
A child who received birth doses but missed Pentavalent-1 is still technically classified as zero-dose in many monitoring frameworks because they haven't entered the routine series.

Implementation of 24/7 birth-dose vaccination services before hospital discharge
Relying solely on mass media campaigns to change cultural traditions
Wait for the 6-week routine EPI visit at the nearest basic health unit
Mandatory school-based vaccination for infants at 9 months of age

24/7 birth-dose centers ensure that the child is immunized immediately after birth while still in the hospital, bypassing the access barrier created by the subsequent 40-day home-stay tradition.
Changing deep-seated cultural traditions via mass media is slow and often less effective than modifying service delivery to accommodate those traditions.
Waiting for 6 weeks misses the critical window for birth doses (BCG, OPV-0) and risks the child remaining unvaccinated during the first month due to cultural isolation practices.
School-based vaccination is for older children (e.g., HPV, Measles-Rubella) and does not address the immediate protection needed for newborns against tuberculosis and polio.

category: Discuss recent developments in the EPI, Pakistan
coreConcept: Recent EPI Birth Dose & MNTE Status
statement: In June 2026, a medical student is rotating in a rural health center in Balochistan. They observe a neonate born 2 hours ago. Based on the most recent EPI developments and the current status of Maternal and Neonatal Tetanus Elimination (MNTE) in Pakistan, which of the following statements is clinically accurate?
options: The newborn must wait 40 days for the first dose of OPV due to traditional postnatal practices
Balochistan has already achieved the MNTE threshold of less than 1 case per 10,000 live births
The neonate should only receive BCG at birth as Hep B is not yet part of any birth-dose program
Maternal tetanus vaccination is no longer required in Balochistan due to national pre-validation
The neonate should receive BCG, OPV-0, and potentially a Hep B birth dose if a 24-hour birth-dose center is available
correctOption: The neonate should receive BCG, OPV-0, and potentially a Hep B birth dose if a 24-hour birth-dose center is available
optionExplanations: The 40-day wait (Chilla) is a cultural barrier that the EPI aims to overcome; medical guidelines mandate birth doses as early as possible to ensure the child is not 'zero-dose'.
The elimination threshold for MNTE is 1 case per 1,000 live births (not 10,000), and Balochistan is the only province that has not yet reached this target as of mid-2026.
Hepatitis B birth dose is being progressively introduced and is already part of 24/7 birth-dose center protocols in many areas as of 2026.
Maternal tetanus vaccination remains critical, especially in Balochistan, which has not yet achieved the elimination threshold, unlike other provinces.
Recent EPI developments emphasize 'birth dose' packages including BCG, OPV-0, and Hep-B administered as soon as possible, ideally before discharge from the facility.

Balochistan remains the province still working toward the [MNTE] target.

category: Discuss recent developments in the EPI, Pakistan
statement: In 2026, the Federal Directorate of Immunization reported the expansion of 24/7 birth-dose centers. What is the strategic clinical advantage of providing BCG, OPV-0, and Hepatitis B vaccines within the first 24 hours at these specialized hospital centers?
options: To prevent loss to follow-up before the mother and child are discharged
To allow for immediate treatment of vaccine-related anaphylaxis in a labor ward
To ensure vaccines are administered before maternal antibodies can interfere
To replace the need for the 6-week Pentavalent dose
To maximize the immune response which is highest only in the first 24 hours
correctOption: To prevent loss to follow-up before the mother and child are discharged
optionExplanations: Providing vaccines before discharge ensures that even if a family is hard to reach or follows the 40-day seclusion tradition, the child has already begun their immunization series.
While safety is important, birth-dose vaccines are extremely safe; the primary strategic reason for these centers is increasing coverage and reducing 'zero-dose' status.
Maternal antibodies actually interfere with some vaccines (like Measles), but BCG and OPV are given at birth regardless; the center's goal is access, not antibody management.
Birth doses (BCG, OPV-0, HepB-0) supplement and prime the schedule; they do not replace the primary series that begins at 6 weeks.
While early protection is good, the immune system remains responsive after 24 hours; the primary driver is operational and logistical rather than a 24-hour physiological peak.

coreConcept: Role of Community Health Workers in Immunization
statement: What is the primary role of Lady Health Workers (LHWs) in the organizational implementation of the EPI to ensure high uptake?
options: Locating zero-dose children, tracing defaulters, and linking households with fixed centers
Replacing the role of the World Health Organization in policy making
Manufacturing vaccines at the district level
Performing specialized cardiac surgeries on infants
Managing the national budget at the Federal Directorate level
correctOption: Locating zero-dose children, tracing defaulters, and linking households with fixed centers
optionExplanations: LHWs provide the vital link between the community and the health system, performing the active field-work necessary to identify and bring under-immunized children into the program.

LHWs implement policy on the ground; they do not replace international health organizations in high-level policy formulation and guidance for the nation and the world as a whole in its pursuit of health and happiness for all and for the world as a whole in its pursuit of health and happiness for all and for the world as a whole in its pursuit of health and happiness for all.
Vaccines are manufactured by specialized pharmaceutical entities, not by community health workers at the district level.
LHWs are community-based primary care workers; they are not surgeons or specialized medical doctors.
Administrative and budgetary management occurs at the Federal and Provincial Directorate levels, not by community-level LHWs.

category: Discuss recent developments in the EPI, Pakistan
statement: Which set of services is characteristic of the newly established 24/7 birth-dose vaccination centers in Pakistan as reported in 2026?
options: Immediate vaccination with BCG, OPV-0, and Hepatitis B, plus referral for subsequent EPI doses.
Administration of Pentavalent and PCV vaccines only.
Vaccination with TCV and MR-1 for all newborns before discharge.
Providing HPV vaccination to mothers during the postnatal period.
Treatment of active neonatal tuberculosis and surgical correction of congenital defects.
correctOption: Immediate vaccination with BCG, OPV-0, and Hepatitis B, plus referral for subsequent EPI doses.
optionExplanations: The birth-dose centers focus on the immediate postnatal vaccines (BCG, OPV-0, Hep-B) to ensure protection before the mother and child leave the hospital facility.
Pentavalent and PCV vaccines are administered starting at 6 weeks of age, not at birth.
TCV and MR-1 are administered at 9 months of age, not at birth.
HPV vaccine is targeted at adolescent girls (9-14 years), not at mothers in birth-dose centers.
EPI centers are for preventive immunization, not for the surgical or medical treatment of active diseases or congenital defects.

category: Discuss recent developments in the EPI, Pakistan
statement: A 2-month-old infant is brought to a primary health center in a peri-urban settlement in Pakistan. The mother reports that the child has received no vaccinations since birth because of a traditional 40-day postpartum home-confinement practice. How should this child be categorized within the EPI framework, and what is the primary marker for this status?
options: Defaulter; marker is failure to attend the 10-week visit
Zero-dose child; marker is lack of the first routine vaccine dose
Fully immunized for age; marker is the 6-week grace period
Partially vaccinated; marker is missing the BCG dose
Hesitant-family child; marker is the 40-day cultural delay
correctOption: Zero-dose child; marker is lack of the first routine vaccine dose
optionExplanations: A 'defaulter' typically refers to someone who started the schedule but missed subsequent doses; this child has never entered the system.
A 'zero-dose' child is defined specifically by the lack of the first routine vaccine (often used as a proxy for healthcare access). This child represents the 'unreached' population.
The child is definitely not fully immunized for age as they have missed birth doses (BCG, OPV-0) and the 6-week doses (Penta-1, etc.).
A child who has received no vaccines is not 'partially' vaccinated; partial vaccination refers to children who started but failed to complete the series.
While 'hesitancy' or cultural practices are the reason, the formal EPI categorization for a child with no vaccines is 'zero-dose'. 'Hesitant-family' is not a formal vaccination status category.

category: Describe the goals and objectives of the Expanded Program of Immunization (EPI) in Pakistan
statement: In the context of EPI objectives, why is 'zero-dose' status used as a critical marker for evaluating program success rather than just the national coverage average?
options: It determines the geographical altitude at which vaccines lose their biological efficacy
It indicates the chemical failure of the first dose of the Pentavalent vaccine in neonates
It serves as a diagnostic tool for identifying genetic resistance to vaccine antigens
It monitors the total number of vaccines wasted due to cold-chain breaches at the federal level
It identifies children who have not received the first routine vaccine as a marker of access to routine immunization
correctOption: It identifies children who have not received the first routine vaccine as a marker of access to routine immunization
optionExplanations: Option D is incorrect because the metric relates to population coverage and service delivery reach, not the physical properties of vaccines at different altitudes.
Option A is incorrect because 'zero-dose' refers to a lack of access/administration, not the pharmacological or chemical failure of a vaccine dose.
Option C is incorrect because 'zero-dose' is an operational and epidemiological metric of coverage, not a clinical or genetic diagnostic test.
Option E is incorrect because wastage rates are monitored separately from the immunization status of individual children (zero-dose status).

Option B is correct. Zero-dose children represent those completely missed by the system. Reaching them is an objective because it measures the program's ability to provide equitable access to underserved or remote populations.

category: Identify the strategies employed to implement the EPI in various communities
statement: Which tool is identified as essential for maintaining continuity of the EPI schedule when a family moves between different healthcare providers or geographic regions?
options: The national identity card (CNIC) of the father
The birth certificate issued by the local union council
The hospital discharge summary for maternal delivery
A verbal history provided by the grandmother
The immunization card (vaccination card)
correctOption: The immunization card (vaccination card)
optionExplanations: The CNIC identifies the parent but contains no clinical data regarding the child's immunization status or pending doses.
The birth certificate records the birth but does not track the specific dates and types of vaccinations administered over the 15-month schedule.
The discharge summary may record the birth dose but will not include subsequent vaccinations (at 6, 10, 14 weeks, 9, and 15 months) administered at different sites.
Verbal histories are often unreliable or incomplete and do not provide the definitive clinical evidence needed for accurate schedule management.
The immunization card is the primary record-keeping tool that travels with the child, allowing any health worker to immediately identify which vaccines have been given and which are due.
citation: In book "Park’s book of preventive & social medicine + latest EPI related guidelines of Pakistan": The vaccination card provides a permanent record of completed and pending doses and remains useful even if the child changes healthcare provider or moves to another area.

category: List the key vaccines included in the EPI schedule
statement: An 11-month-old child is brought to a clinic in Balochistan. The history reveals the child received BCG and OPV at birth but has had no other vaccinations since then. According to the EPI guidelines, which of the following represents the most urgent set of vaccines to be administered to begin catching up with the schedule?
options: Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, and Rotavirus-1
Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, Rotavirus-1, and MR-1
TCV and MR-2 only.
MR-1 and TCV only, as the child is past the age for Pentavalent.
Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, and MR-1
correctOption: Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, and Rotavirus-1
optionExplanations: Correct. For a child who has missed all doses since birth, the schedule begins with the 6-week vaccines (Pentavalent-1, OPV-1, PCV-1, and Rotavirus-1). Even though the child is 11 months old, these primary doses are essential to build baseline immunity.

Incorrect. While technically multiple vaccines can be given, the standard practice is to start the earliest missed series first. Note: Rotavirus vaccine has specific age limits (usually not started after 15-32 weeks depending on the brand/local guidelines), but according to the provided text, the 6-week dose is the next logical step.
Incorrect. MR-2 is only given at 15 months, and the child hasn't even received MR-1 yet.
Incorrect. Children should not be denied the primary Pentavalent series just because they are older; they remain susceptible to Diphtheria, Pertussis, and Tetanus.

Incorrect. While MR-1 is due at 9 months, the child first needs the primary series of Pentavalent, OPV, and PCV to be initiated. However, usually, MR-1 can be given alongside these, but this option lacks Rotavirus-1 which is still indicated for a child under 1 year.

Missed children should be identified and brought back into the schedule so that the required doses can be completed.

category: Describe the goals and objectives of the Expanded Program of Immunization (EPI) in Pakistan
statement: A 10-month-old child from a nomadic community in Balochistan is identified by a mobile health team. The child has never received any vaccinations. According to EPI objectives and surveillance terminology, how is this child classified and what is the immediate programmatic priority?
options: Partially vaccinated; priority is to restart the entire schedule from the beginning
Ineligible child; priority is to wait until the next birth cohort starts
Defaulted child; priority is to investigate the healthcare worker responsible
Zero-dose child; priority is to use this child as a marker of access to routine immunization
High-risk carrier; priority is immediate quarantine before vaccination
correctOption: Zero-dose child; priority is to use this child as a marker of access to routine immunization
optionExplanations: A child who has never received a vaccine is 'zero-dose,' not 'partially vaccinated.' Reaching them is about establishing access, not just restarting a schedule.
No child is 'ineligible' for their required doses; sustained immunization is essential as every child is part of a susceptible group until vaccinated.
While tracing is important, the term 'zero-dose' is the specific surveillance marker used to measure total lack of access, which is the primary concern here.
Zero-dose children are critical indicators of 'failed access' to health services; reaching them is a central priority to ensure equity and interrupt transmission.
The EPI focuses on preventive vaccination rather than quarantine, which is a different public health protocol for active outbreaks.

category: Identify the common barriers to immunization coverage in Pakistan
statement: In the context of the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) in Pakistan, which term is specifically used to classify children who have not received the first routine vaccine used as a primary marker of access to services?
options: Hard-to-reach children
Zero-dose children
Defaulted children
Partially immunized children
Missed-opportunity children
correctOption: Zero-dose children
optionExplanations: Hard-to-reach children refers to populations geographically or socially isolated, which is a reason for being zero-dose, but not the definition of the vaccination status itself.

Zero-dose children are defined specifically as those who have not received any routine vaccines, specifically the initial dose (like BCG or Penta1) that serves as a proxy for access to the health system.
Defaulted children refers to those who attended one or more sessions but did not return for subsequent scheduled doses, resulting in an incomplete series.
Partially immunized children are those who have initiated the vaccination series but failed to complete the full schedule according to their age group.
Missed-opportunity children are those who visited a health facility for other reasons but were not screened or provided with due vaccines during that encounter.

category: Describe enhance vaccination uptake
statement: In the context of evaluating Pakistan's routine immunization access and identifying targets for improved uptake, how is a 'zero-dose child' defined?
options: A child who has not received the first routine vaccine used as a marker of access to routine immunization.
A child whose parents have signed a formal refusal form for all types of medical interventions.
A child residing in a household where the Lady Health Worker has never visited.
A child who has received only the OPV-0 dose but no other vaccines.
A child who has completed the primary series but missed the 15-month MR-2 booster.
correctOption: A child who has not received the first routine vaccine used as a marker of access to routine immunization.
optionExplanations: Zero-dose children represent the most underserved population; their lack of the very first marker vaccine indicates they have no access to the health system's routine services.
While a zero-dose child might have parents who refuse, the definition is based on the objective status of having received no routine vaccines, not the administrative status of a refusal form.
Lack of LHW visits may be a reason for zero-dose status, but it is not the definition itself; the definition is purely clinical/immunological recording.
A child who has received any routine vaccine, even just OPV-0, is no longer strictly considered 'zero-dose' by the programmatic definition of access.
A child who missed only the last booster is considered 'partially vaccinated' or a 'dropout', not a zero-dose child.
